title: Misclassified routing backoff caused cross-region escalation and variant mismatches
creator: Kai Huang
description: Summary: During a capacity surge in us-west-2 on 2026-02-24 we observed repeated cross-region escalations and a steady increase in incorrect model-variant selections. The immediate user-visible impact was a surge in 503s and elevated tail latency for chat generation and embeddings for several enterprise tenants. Investigation showed a misclassification in the routing backoff evaluator that marked healthy hosts as 'backoff' eligible and triggered aggressive cross-region failover and retrying, which in turn caused stale variant mappings to be applied downstream.
timeline:
2026-02-24 02:17 UTC - First alert: 95th percentile latency spike for hosted API in us-west-2.
2026-02-24 02:22 UTC - Automated reroute to us-east-1 begins; error rates in us-east-1 begin to increase.
2026-02-24 02:29 UTC - Routing service logs show backoff-evaluator flipping healthy pool nodes into backoff set due to incorrect evaluation of load metric (metric name mismatch).
2026-02-24 02:35 UTC - Repeated retries triggered remote variant resolution path which returned default legacy quantized variant for several requests.
2026-02-24 03:05 UTC - On-call disabled cross-region reroute policy as emergency mitigation.
2026-02-24 04:10 UTC - Full mitigation in place: routing backoff evaluator updated to correct metric name and retry window increased.
2026-02-25 09:00 UTC - Root cause confirmed and rollback plan drafted.
2026-03-10 11:30 UTC - Postmortem draft ready and action items assigned.
root_cause: A recent config change (cfg-service/optimize-backoff v2) renamed an internal metric from 'request_load.v2' to 'request_load_v2'. The backoff evaluator used the old metric name and defaulted to 'unavailable' which was treated as exceeding the backoff threshold. As a result, healthy hosts in the primary region were temporarily placed into the backoff set. Smart routing then performed cross-region escalations and retries. The retry/fallback path incorrectly resolved model variants using a stale mapping cache that had not been primed for cross-region variant compatibility, so some requests were routed to incompatible legacy quantized variants, increasing error rates and latency.
detection: Detection was via automated SLO alerting for p95 latency and a spike in 5xx rate. On-call dashboards showed a gap between host health and backoff decisions. We detected the metric name mismatch through correlation of config changes in cfg-service audit logs and the onset of backoff-evaluator decisions. Traces showed repeated cross-region hops and variant resolution calls immediately prior to client-facing errors.
immediate_actions: Disabled automatic cross-region reroutes (temporary mitigation) - completed 2026-02-24 03:05 UTC
Rolled back cfg-service/optimize-backoff to previous revision until evaluator logic was patched - completed 2026-02-24 04:10 UTC
Primed variant resolution cache in us-east-1 with compatible variant mappings for affected models - completed 2026-02-24 04:25 UTC
Open incident channel and notify top 10 affected tenants with summary and ETA - completed 2026-02-24 05:00 UTC
action_items: ENG - Patch backoff-evaluator to tolerate missing metrics and fallback to recent values instead of treating as exceed-threshold (owner: Tomás Rivera, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-03
ENG - Add unit and integration tests for metric-name drift in cfg-service and enforce schema validation on metric keys (owner: Morgan Lee, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-10
ENG - Update routing runbooks to include a safe-mode that throttles cross-region reroutes instead of disabling them entirely (owner: Aisha Patel, estimate: 5) - due 2026-03-17
ENG - Implement variant-resolution priming as part of cross-region failover flow, with explicit compatibility checks (owner: Evelyn Brooks, estimate: 8) - due 2026-04-01
SRE - Add a dedicated SLO for cross-region reroute rate and create dashboards/alerts for abnormal reroute frequency (owner: Priya Nair, estimate: 3) - due 2026-03-05
PM - Communicate post-incident summary and interim mitigations to impacted customers and update status page template (owner: Rowan Smith, estimate: 2) - due 2026-03-04
verification_plan:
1) Run synthetic traffic that triggers the backoff-evaluator edge cases with metric names intentionally missing and verify the evaluator falls back to recent values instead of marking host as backoff.
2) Simulate region capacity surge in staging and ensure cross-region reroute throttling prevents rapid cascade; confirm variant priming completes before traffic shifts.
3) Deploy canary with new tests enabled against a subset of routing instances and monitor cross-region reroute SLO for 72 hours.
4) Run chaos job that renames one metric in a test cfg-service and assert schema validation blocks the change.
postmortem_notes: Lessons learned: 1) Small config key renames are high-risk if evaluators treat missing metrics as failures instead of unknown. 2) Cross-region reroutes need throttling and explicit variant compatibility checks. 3) Observability gaps: add tighter linking between config audit logs and routing decision traces. Retro feedback: include PMs earlier for communication cadence, and add an incident-specific checklist to routing runbooks.
